newsitem.title: USA: Dow closes above 6,000-level for first time ever.
newsitem.headline: Dow closes above 6,000-level for first time ever.

text.p: The Dow Industrials reached a significant milestone on Monday, unofficially closing above the key psychological 6000 level for the first time ever.
The Dow Industrials ended up 40.99 to close at 6010, helped by oil stocks that were buoyed by crude prices that hit their a new post-Gulf War.

"A lot of players are on a long weekend," said Peggy Farley, managing director at Amas Securities. "The folks who are left are pretty bullish. There's a general bullishness in the market, nothing to drive the market down today."
On Monday, U.S. stocks had no clues from the bond markets, which were closed due to the Columbus Day holiday.
Last week, the Dow topped 6,000 during intraday trading, but never finished above the mark.
"It's simply momentum carryover from late last week," said Ricky Harrington, technical analyst at Interstate/Johnson.
Analysts said that recent economic news, including the producer price index report last Friday, indicates that inflation remains in check, and that was enough to keep investors bullish.
Texaco shares reached a 52-week, closing up 3-5/8 to 101-3/4. Mobil added 1-3/8 to 118-1/2, Royal Dutch ADRs gained 1-3/4 to 164-3/4, Exxon rose 1-1/4 to 87-5/8, and Chevron rose 1-1/8 to 66-7/8.
Harrington estimated that the gains racked up by Texaco, Chevron and Exxon added about 20 points to the Dow index.

Oil prices pinched the Dow Jones Transports, which ended off 13.42 to 20.62.47. Airline stocks were especially hurt, with AMR Corp, parent of American Airlines, dropped 2-5/8 to 82-3/4, UAL Corp, United airlines parent, fell 1-1/2 to 43-7/8, and Northwest Air shed one to 31-7/8.
Chrysler rose one to 32-3/4. The carmaker reported third quarter profit of $680 million, or $0.93 per diluted share.
The report set a new third quarter profit record, and exceeded Wall Street estimates.

Technology and cyclical stocks also drove the markets. Among the big winners, Intel gained 2-1/4 to 107-5/8. After the markets closed, the chipmaking giant reported third quarter earnings of $1.48 per share, easily topping the First Call analysts' estimate of $1.25.
Also, Gateway 2000 up 3-5/8 to 53-3/8, Dell Computer jumping 4-1/4 to 84-7/8, and Sun Micro adding 1-1/2 to 68-3/8.
Thrifty Payless jumped three to 21-3/8 after rival drugstore chain Rite Aid announced it was buying Thrifty in a stock swap deal, offering 0.65 Rite Aid shares for Thrifty share.
Money center bank stocks were broadly higher, in advance of an earnings report expected on Tuesday from Chase Manhattan. Chase gained one to 82-1/2.
Among consumer non-durable stocks, Gillette was up 1-3/4 to 74-7/8, and Johnson and Johnson rose one to 52-1/2.
Cascade Communications jumped 3-1/2 to 74-7/8. UBS Securities set a "minimum" nine-month price target of $80.
Among other major indices, the S&P 500 closed up 2.88 to 703.54, the New York Composite Index gained 1.34 to 374.23, and the Value Line index gained 1.17 to 647.32.
